data.body:
EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION of this ticket's premise, from the change that motivated it.

Gerrit 1189 (`03b0`) took `LLM-Review -1` tagged `coverage-gap (review-error)` on patch set 1, with
`Verified +1` alongside it — CI green, review bot unable to run. Patch set 2 was then pushed (for an
unrelated reason: a guard-order improvement) and the review bot returned **`LLM-Review +1`**.

Two things this establishes:

1. **The `-1` really was transient infrastructure, not the diff.** The substantive content of the
   change was unaltered in the parts the first review would have examined, and the second review
   passed. So the fail-closed veto did exactly its job — it blocked on "I could not establish
   coverage" rather than on a finding — and the correct remedy was indeed a re-run.

2. **A re-trigger mechanism has to be a no-op re-run, not "push a new patch set".** The only reason
   this recovered is that I happened to have a further change to push. A contributor with a finished,
   correct change and no further edits has nothing to push, and the only options today are to
   fabricate an empty patch set or wait for a maintainer. That is precisely the gap this ticket
   closes, and it is worth stating in the acceptance criteria that the trigger must NOT require a new
   revision — re-reviewing the SAME patch set is the point.

Also worth noting for whoever implements this: the two labels behaved INDEPENDENTLY and correctly
throughout — `Verified` stayed +1 across both patch sets while `LLM-Review` went -1 then +1. So the
re-trigger only needs to touch the review leg, and must not disturb or re-run the `Verified` leg.
